text:
sam: Quick sync: product reported a support ticket where a tenant saw an apparent 2x spike after enabling v2 canary. Turns out our console histogram was double-counting fallback paths. We should fix upstream telemetry semantics, not just band-aid the UX.
leah: Agreed. Can we standardize on one canonical variant field that the billing and analytics pipelines trust? Right now we emit: `variant_attempts: [v1, v2]` and `final_variant: v2` which some downstream consumers ignore.
omar: Context: we emit multiple events during routing: handshake (client advertises v1), decision (router chooses v2), and response (served v2). Some systems index the handshake and decision events which inflates counts.
ingest-bot: note: reindexing historical data is expensive. We should avoid breaking existing billing export schema.
console-pm: From the console side, product wants three things for rollouts: 1) accurate billed tokens per logical route, 2) breakdown of % fallbacks over time, 3) an "impact simulator" that estimates monthly cost if the route flips to X.
sam: Proposal: 1) Introduce `canonical_served_variant` on the response event only (single emitter). 2) Keep handshake/decision events for debug but mark them with `debug_only: true` so ingestion can drop them for billing paths. 3) Add an ingestion-layer transform: when billing pipeline consumes events, prefer `canonical_served_variant` if present; otherwise fall back to legacy mapping.
leah: That solves the double-counting. Also we need to avoid exploding logs during deprecation handshakes. Currently we sample handshake events at 100% which floods our debug cluster.
omar: Let's design adaptive sampling rules: - If tenant QPS >= 10rps and rollout_percentage >= 1%, sample handshake events at 1%. - If tenant QPS < 10rps, sample at 100% for that tenant while the rollout is active. - If the tenant is flagged as "sensitive" (enterprise), always sample 100%.
ingest-bot: Implementation detail: sampling decisions must happen at the router after we know tenant id and rollout metadata. Router already tags events with `rollout_tag` so we can apply deterministic sampling based on a hash of tenant_id + day. That keeps the sample stable across retries.
console-pm: For the impact simulator: we need per-route token distribution. After canonical_served_variant exists, we will have clean histograms. For now we can compute a provisional delta by taking `avg_tokens_per_request` from last 7 days and multiplying by model cost-per-token. Add a confidence band to indicate noise.
harry: Edgecases: 1) legacy clients that don't send `X-Client-Version` and 2) multi-model fallbacks (e.g., route -> llama2-small then -> llama2-large). How do we represent canonical_variant? It might need fields: `variant_id`, `model_id`, `quantization_profile`.
sam: Suggest canonical_served_variant be a flattened string for billing "model=llama2-13b|variant=v2|q=8bit" and also emit a machine-readable debug blob `served_variant_meta` for observability consumers. Billing pipeline reads only the flattened string.
leah: That's fine, but keep in mind the JSON shape in billing exports must not change. We can add a new column `served_variant_flat` and populate it; existing `variant_id` keeps value for backwards compatibility.
omar: Operational: we should add a console flag "Show raw routing events (experimental)" that reads from the debug store (pre-de-dupe) so platform engineers can inspect why a tenant saw fallbacks. Keep behind an admin toggle.
ingest-bot: Canary plan: deploy router change to emit `canonical_served_variant` and `debug_only` markers to staging. Enable ingestion transform in staging and run a 48h side-by-side where billing reads both legacy and canonical, compare totals. If diffs < 0.1% for top 100 tenants, schedule prod rollout.
console-pm: UX tasks: - Mock impact simulator using provisional numbers (label as "estimate"). - Add a tooltip explaining canonical_served_variant and confidence. - Add a per-route toggle for experimental raw-events view.
harry: Data retention: handshake debug events can be set to 7d/30d retention tiers. Let's not retain them long by default.
sam: Action items (owners): 1) Emit canonical_served_variant in router responses (omar/sam) 2) Ingestion: implement transform that maps canonical->billing column and filters debug_only for billing (leah/ingest-bot) 3) Sampling: implement adaptive sampling rules in router (omar/ingest-bot) 4) Console: provisional impact simulator + toggle + tooltip (console-pm) 5) Runbook updates and canary (sam/harry).
leah: Timeline? If we scope to non-breaking additions (new fields, new billing column), I can land ingestion changes in 10 days. Router changes ~1 week. Console mockups 5 days. End-to-end canary start in 2 weeks.
omar: Router PR notes: deterministic sample = hash(tenant_id + rollout_id) % 10000 < sample_rate_basis_points. Will share code snippet in PR.
console-pm: I'll schedule a demo with product ops after the 48h staging run. We should also notify support docs so they don't escalate these billing "spikes" during rollout.
ingest-bot: I'll create the staging job and a query that calculates canonical_vs_legacy delta by tenant and route.
harry: small ask: include a human-readable "why" in the console for any simulated impact: e.g., "Estimate assumes 100% traffic -> v2, model pricing = $0.0006/token, sample window = last 30d".
sam: Great. I'll open the router PR with schema examples. tagging: @omar @leah @ingest-bot @console-pm @harry.
console-pm: Thanks all. I'll drop mock screenshots into the design thread and link to this convo. :rocket:
